# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

1 | # Culprit — Product Specification v1.0
2 | 
3 | ## 1. Purpose
4 | Culprit is a Python CLI tool built on IBM Bob 2.0 that debugs live
5 | backend services and multi-codebase projects. Given running endpoints
6 | + source code, it authenticates, reproduces the failure at runtime,
7 | traces the root cause across codebases, generates a verified fix, and
8 | writes a regression test.
9 | 
10 | Culprit combines RUNTIME evidence (real HTTP calls, real responses,
11 | real errors) with STATIC evidence (source code across N codebases) —
12 | this is the differentiator vs static-only AI debuggers.
13 | 
14 | ## 2. Command-line interface
15 | 
16 |     culprit debug [inputs...] --issue "<description>"
17 | 
18 |     Input flags (at least one code source + optionally a live URL):
19 |       --url URL              Live endpoint to probe (repeatable)
20 |       --folder PATH          Local code folder (repeatable, 1-6)
21 |       --git URL              Remote repo to clone (repeatable, 1-4)
22 | 
23 |     Auth flags (choose one when --url is used):
24 |       --auth-bearer          Reads BEARER_TOKEN from .env
25 |       --auth-basic           Reads BASIC_USER, BASIC_PASS from .env
26 |       --auth-oauth2          Reads OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET,
27 |                              OAUTH_TOKEN_URL from .env
28 |       --auth-apikey          Reads API_KEY, API_KEY_HEADER from .env
29 |       --no-auth              Explicit for public endpoints
30 | 
31 |     Behavior flags:
32 |       --issue TEXT           Bug description (required)
33 |       --trace PATH           Optional: path to a stack trace / error log
34 |       --dry-run              Analyze only; no fix applied, no commit
35 | 
36 | ## 3. Hard limits (deterministic — NOT decided by AI)
37 | Defined in src/culprit/config.py:
38 | 
39 |     MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
40 |     MAX_WALLCLOCK_SECONDS = 240
41 |     MAX_FILES_PER_SUBAGENT = 25
42 |     MAX_CODEBASES = 6
43 |     MAX_URLS = 3
44 |     MAX_BOBCOIN_PER_RUN = 8
45 |     CONFIDENCE_FLOOR = 0.70
46 |     HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 15
47 |     AUTH_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 300
48 | 
49 | ## 4. Domain model (Pydantic — schema-enforced)
50 | 
51 |     class Endpoint:
52 |         url: str
53 |         method: str
54 |         headers: dict
55 |         expected_status: int
56 |         actual_status: Optional[int]
57 | 
58 |     class AuthContext:
59 |         scheme: BEARER | BASIC | OAUTH2 | APIKEY | NONE
60 |         token: Optional[str]  # never logged, never in report
61 |         expires_at: Optional[datetime]
62 | 
63 |     class RuntimeEvidence:
64 |         endpoint: Endpoint
65 |         request_body: Optional[str]
66 |         response_body: str
67 |         response_status: int
68 |         latency_ms: float
69 |         stack_trace_hint: Optional[str]
70 | 
71 |     class SourceCodebase:
72 |         name: str
73 |         root_path: Path
74 |         language: str
75 |         entry_points: list[str]
76 | 
77 |     class Bug:
78 |         description: str
79 |         runtime_evidence: list[RuntimeEvidence]
80 |         static_evidence: list[SourceCodebase]
81 | 
82 |     class RootCause:
83 |         codebase: str
84 |         file: str
85 |         line: int
86 |         symbol: str
87 |         explanation: str
88 |         confidence: float  # 0.0 - 1.0
89 | 
90 |     class Fix:
91 |         target_codebase: str
92 |         unified_diff: str
93 |         applied_files: list[str]
94 | 
95 |     class RegressionTest:
96 |         codebase: str
97 |         file: str
98 |         test_name: str
99 |         code: str
100 | 
101 |     class Attempt:
102 |         num: int
103 |         subagent_outputs: dict
104 |         test_result: Optional[TestResult]
105 |         failure_reason: Optional[str]
106 | 
107 |     class CulpritReport:
108 |         status: FIXED | PARTIAL | NEEDS_HUMAN
109 |         bug: Bug
110 |         root_cause: Optional[RootCause]   # None if run aborted before tracing
111 |         fix: Optional[Fix]
112 |         regression_test: Optional[RegressionTest]
113 |         attempts: list[Attempt]
114 |         elapsed_seconds: float
115 |         bobcoins_used: float
116 |         adjudications: list[Adjudication]   # see §12
117 |         adjudicator_available: bool         # False if watsonx.ai was unreachable
118 | 
119 | ## 5. Subagents (Strategy pattern; each has a specific output type)
120 | 
121 |     Reproducer(workspace, bug) -> FailingTest
122 |       * If --url provided: the orchestrator has already probed it; the
123 |         captured RuntimeEvidence is given to Reproducer as context
124 |       * ALWAYS writes a pytest that exercises the code path IN-PROCESS
125 |         (e.g. Flask test_client), never the live URL — a running server
126 |         keeps old code loaded, so a live-URL test cannot see a fix
127 |       * The bug is "observable" only if this test FAILS on current code
128 | 
129 |     CauseTracer(workspace, bug, runtime_evidence) -> RootCause
130 |       * Walks source code across ALL codebases
131 |       * Follows imports/API contracts between codebases
132 |       * Correlates runtime response with source lines
133 |       * Assigns confidence 0.0-1.0
134 | 
135 |     FixAuthor(workspace, root_cause) -> list[Fix]
136 |       * Proposes up to 3 candidate patches
137 |       * Ranked by risk (quick patch < proper fix < refactor)
138 | 
139 |     Guard(workspace, root_cause, fix) -> RegressionTest
140 |       * Writes a pytest that would have caught this bug
141 |       * Never touches the fix code itself
142 | 
143 | ## 6. Self-healing orchestrator loop
144 | 
145 |     workspace = load(folders, git_urls)
146 |     auth = build_auth_context(auth_flag)  # from env vars only
147 | 
148 |     for attempt in range(MAX_ATTEMPTS):
149 |         runtime_evidence = probe_url(url, auth) if url else None
150 |         parallel_run(Reproducer, CauseTracer)   # both use runtime_evidence
151 |         if failing_test passes on current code:
152 |             return NEEDS_HUMAN (BugNotObservable, E9)
153 |         if confidence < CONFIDENCE_FLOOR:
154 |             return NEEDS_HUMAN
155 |         candidates = FixAuthor(root_cause)       # up to 3, lowest risk first
156 |         fix = first candidate whose adjudication == APPROVE   # §12; fail-open
157 |         if no candidate approved:
158 |             record failure  # reasoning feeds next attempt as context
159 |             continue        # no fix is EVER applied without approval
160 |         regression_test = Guard(root_cause, fix)
161 |         apply(fix + regression_test)
162 |         result = test_runner.run(all_codebases)
163 |         if result.passed:
164 |             git.commit(fix + regression_test)
165 |             return FIXED
166 |         revert(fix)
167 |         record failure  # feeds next attempt as context
168 | 
169 |     return NEEDS_HUMAN
170 | 
171 | ## 7. Edge cases (explicit — every one has a defined behavior)
172 | 
173 |     E1  No tests in any codebase -> skip Guard, status = PARTIAL
174 |     E2  Bob returns malformed JSON -> pydantic error -> one retry
175 |         inside bob_client -> then SubagentError
176 |     E3  Fix breaks other tests -> revert, next attempt gets failure log
177 |     E4  Bobcoin budget exhausted -> BudgetExhausted -> status = PARTIAL
178 |     E5  Confidence < 0.70 -> DO NOT apply fix -> NEEDS_HUMAN
179 |     E6  --dry-run -> subagents run, no apply, no commit
180 |     E7  Auth token acquisition fails -> AuthError -> abort, no partial
181 |     E8  URL unreachable (timeout/DNS) -> UnreachableError -> abort
182 |     E9  Reproducer's failing test PASSES on current code (bug not
183 |         reproducible) -> BugNotObservable -> NEEDS_HUMAN with a message
184 |         asking for a better --issue text. NOTE: an HTTP 200 alone is NOT
185 |         E9 — a wrong value returned with 200 is a real bug.
186 |     E10 Bug spans codebases we don't have -> NEEDS_HUMAN with message
187 |         naming the missing codebase
188 | 
189 | ## 8. Where AI adds value (defensible in interview)
190 | 
191 |     - Semantic mapping between runtime response and source lines
192 |       across N codebases (no static analyzer can do this)
193 |     - Natural language --issue -> concrete failing pytest
194 |     - Root cause reasoning that ties HTTP response payload
195 |       to specific lines in specific files across services
196 | 
197 | ## 9. Where deterministic code decides (NOT AI)
198 | 
199 |     - Loop control (retry count, budget)
200 |     - HTTP client (requests, timeouts, retries)
201 |     - Auth flow (token acquisition, refresh, TTL)
202 |     - Test execution and result parsing
203 |     - Git operations (commit, diff, revert)
204 |     - Pydantic schema validation
205 |     - Adjudication total score and APPROVE/REJECT verdict (threshold compare)
206 | 
207 | ## 10. Secrets policy (hard rule)
208 | 
209 |     - All credentials live in .env, referenced by env var name
210 |     - .env is git-ignored AND bob-ignored (verified in Step 3)
211 |     - Tokens NEVER appear in report objects, log lines, or Bob
212 |       chat context
213 |     - bob_client.py redacts headers containing 'Authorization',
214 |       'X-API-Key', 'Cookie' before sending prompts to Bob
215 | 
216 | ## 11. Demo scenario (for video)
217 | 
218 |     Multi-service e-commerce sample:
219 |       sample_app/frontend  (Flask, calls backend)
220 |       sample_app/backend   (Flask, /cart/total endpoint)
221 |       sample_app/shared    (pricing library)
222 | 
223 |     Seeded bug: pricing library applies discount pre-tax,
224 |     frontend expects post-tax discount.
225 | 
226 |     Demo run:
227 |       culprit debug \
228 |         --url http://localhost:8000/cart/total \
229 |         --auth-bearer \
230 |         --folder ./sample_app/frontend \
231 |         --folder ./sample_app/backend \
232 |         --folder ./sample_app/shared \
233 |         --issue "cart total wrong when discount code applied"
234 | 
235 | ## 12. watsonx.ai Adjudicator (second opinion)
236 | 
237 |     Model:    read from WATSONX_MODEL_ID (a Granite model listed in the
238 |               hackathon "watsonx Hackathon Sandbox" project, Dallas region).
239 |               Never llama-3-405b-instruct or mistral-* (out of scope per
240 |               hackathon guide).
241 |     Transport: plain REST via httpx (IAM token endpoint + watsonx.ai
242 |               text/chat endpoint). No ibm-watsonx-ai SDK: keeps deps light
243 |               and avoids Python-version compatibility risk.
244 |     Endpoint: WATSONX_URL (default https://us-south.ml.cloud.ibm.com)
245 |     Project:  WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
246 |     Auth:     IBM_CLOUD_API_KEY from .env -> IAM token -> watsonx bearer
247 |               (secrets policy of §10 applies: never logged, never in the
248 |               report, never in Bob chat context)
249 | 
250 |     Role: independent critic. Reads (root_cause, the fix selected for this
251 |     attempt, relevant source context) and scores it on three axes:
252 |       - correctness  (does the fix actually address the root cause?)
253 |       - safety       (does the fix introduce new risks?)
254 |       - minimalism   (is it the smallest change that works?)
255 | 
256 |     class Adjudication:
257 |         correctness_score: float   # 0.0 - 1.0   (from the model)
258 |         safety_score: float        # 0.0 - 1.0   (from the model)
259 |         minimalism_score: float    # 0.0 - 1.0   (from the model)
260 |         total_score: float         # mean of the 3 axes (computed by code)
261 |         verdict: APPROVE | REJECT  # total_score >= threshold (computed by code)
262 |         reasoning: str             # from the model
263 | 
264 |     The model only produces the three axis scores and the reasoning.
265 |     total_score and verdict are computed deterministically by code.
266 |     Model output is schema-enforced via the Adjudication pydantic model.
267 | 
268 |     Hard constants (defined in src/culprit/config.py):
269 | 
270 |         ADJUDICATION_THRESHOLD = 0.65    # total_score below this -> REJECT
271 |         WATSONX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 20
272 |         WATSONX_MAX_RETRIES = 2
273 | 
274 |     Behavior:
275 |       * REJECT -> the fix is NOT applied; the reasoning is recorded as the
276 |         attempt's failure_reason and fed to the next attempt (§6).
277 |       * watsonx failure, timeout, or missing credentials -> log a warning
278 |         and proceed WITHOUT adjudication; report.adjudicator_available =
279 |         false. Never block on infrastructure failure.
280 |       * Malformed model output -> pydantic error -> one retry -> then
281 |         treated as a watsonx failure (previous bullet).
282 |       * Source context sent to watsonx passes through the same redaction
283 |         as bob_client (§10).
284 |       * --dry-run -> adjudication still runs and is reported; nothing is
285 |         applied and nothing is committed (E6).
286 | 
287 |     New edge case:
288 |       E11  Every attempt REJECTed -> NEEDS_HUMAN, with the last
289 |            adjudication reasoning included in the report.
290 | 
291 | ## 13. Where each model adds value (defensible answer)
292 | 
293 |     Bob subagents: repository-aware, multi-file semantic reasoning; Agent
294 |       mode for tool use (git, tests, filesystem).
295 | 
296 |     watsonx.ai Granite: an independent second opinion on proposed fixes,
297 |       reducing single-model blind spots; produces structured axis scores.
298 | 
299 |     Deterministic code: budget, HTTP, git, schema validation, loops,
300 |       adjudication total and verdict.
301 | 
302 | ## 14. Bob runtime integration (how Culprit calls Bob)
303 | 
304 |     Culprit's subagents call IBM Bob through Bob Shell in non-interactive
305 |     mode, as a subprocess (bob_client.py):
306 | 
307 |         bob run --format json --mode <ask|agent> --workspace <path>
308 |                 --max-cost <remaining budget> --accept-license "<prompt>"
309 | 
310 |     * Auth: Bob Shell's own login (SSO) or BOB_API_KEY in the environment.
311 |       Culprit never reads, logs or passes BOB_API_KEY itself.
312 |     * Budget: --max-cost is set per call to
313 |       MAX_BOBCOIN_PER_RUN - bobcoins_used so far (hard cap enforced by Bob
314 |       AND by Culprit). Cost per call is read from the JSON output if present.
315 |     * The target service's AuthContext is NEVER passed to bob_client.
316 |     * Prerequisite: Node.js >= 24 and Bob Shell installed.
317 | 
318 |     Bob IDE is used to BUILD Culprit (task sessions exported to
319 |     bob_sessions/ for judging); Bob Shell is used by Culprit at RUNTIME.
320 | 
321 | ## 15. Hackathon MVP scope (deadline-driven)
322 | 
323 |     MUST (demo path):
324 |       --folder (1-6), --url (1), --auth-bearer, --no-auth, --issue,
325 |       --dry-run; 4 subagents via Bob Shell; watsonx.ai adjudicator
326 |       (fail-open); apply -> pytest -> commit; Rich terminal report.
327 | 
328 |     STRETCH (only if time remains; keep stubs raising NotImplementedError):
329 |       --git, --auth-basic, --auth-oauth2, --auth-apikey, --trace.
330 |

"""
Culprit domain models (Pydantic v2).

Defines the canonical data shapes for all Culprit concepts:
Endpoint, AuthContext, RuntimeEvidence, SourceCodebase, Bug,
RootCause, Fix, RegressionTest, Attempt, CulpritReport (§4),
and Adjudication (§12).

These models are the only permitted way to pass structured data
between layers. Credentials (tokens) are present as Optional fields
but are excluded from serialisation via model_config.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator

# ── Enums ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


class AuthScheme(str, Enum):
    """Authentication scheme supported by the CLI (§2)."""

    BEARER = "BEARER"
    BASIC = "BASIC"
    OAUTH2 = "OAUTH2"
    APIKEY = "APIKEY"
    NONE = "NONE"


class ReportStatus(str, Enum):
    """Final status of a Culprit debug run (§4)."""

    FIXED = "FIXED"
    PARTIAL = "PARTIAL"
    NEEDS_HUMAN = "NEEDS_HUMAN"


class AdjudicationVerdict(str, Enum):
    """Deterministic verdict produced by code from total_score (§12)."""

    APPROVE = "APPROVE"
    REJECT = "REJECT"


# ── §4 Models ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


class Endpoint(BaseModel):
    """A live HTTP endpoint to probe (§4)."""

    url: str
    method: str
    headers: dict[str, str]
    expected_status: int
    actual_status: Optional[int] = None


class AuthContext(BaseModel):
    """
    Holds the resolved authentication state for a run (§4).

    token is excluded from all serialisation to enforce §10.
    """

    scheme: AuthScheme
    token: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, exclude=True)
    expires_at: Optional[datetime] = None


class RuntimeEvidence(BaseModel):
    """Captured HTTP interaction evidence from a live endpoint probe (§4)."""

    endpoint: Endpoint
    request_body: Optional[str] = None
    response_body: str
    response_status: int
    latency_ms: float
    stack_trace_hint: Optional[str] = None


class SourceCodebase(BaseModel):
    """A single local codebase made available to subagents (§4)."""

    name: str
    root_path: Path
    language: str
    entry_points: list[str]


class Bug(BaseModel):
    """The problem statement assembled from CLI inputs (§4)."""

    description: str
    runtime_evidence: list[RuntimeEvidence]
    static_evidence: list[SourceCodebase]


class RootCause(BaseModel):
    """Root cause identified by CauseTracer, with a confidence score (§4)."""

    codebase: str
    file: str
    line: int
    symbol: str
    explanation: str
    confidence: float  # 0.0 – 1.0


class Fix(BaseModel):
    """A single candidate patch produced by FixAuthor (§4)."""

    target_codebase: str
    unified_diff: str
    applied_files: list[str]


class RegressionTest(BaseModel):
    """A pytest that would have caught this bug, written by Guard (§4)."""

    codebase: str
    file: str
    test_name: str
    code: str


class TestResult(BaseModel):
    """Outcome of running pytest across all codebases (§6, §9)."""

    __test__ = False  # stop pytest from trying to collect this class

    passed: bool
    output: str
    failed_tests: list[str]


class Attempt(BaseModel):
    """Record of one self-healing loop iteration (§4)."""

    num: int
    subagent_outputs: dict[str, object]
    test_result: Optional[TestResult] = None
    failure_reason: Optional[str] = None


# ── §12 Model ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


class Adjudication(BaseModel):
    """
    watsonx.ai Adjudicator result for one fix candidate (§12).

    correctness_score, safety_score, minimalism_score, and reasoning
    come from the model. total_score and verdict are computed by code.
    """

    correctness_score: float  # 0.0 – 1.0, from model
    safety_score: float       # 0.0 – 1.0, from model
    minimalism_score: float   # 0.0 – 1.0, from model
    total_score: float        # mean of three axes, computed by code
    verdict: AdjudicationVerdict   # threshold compare, computed by code
    reasoning: str            # from model

    @field_validator("correctness_score", "safety_score", "minimalism_score", "total_score")
    @classmethod
    def _score_range(cls, v: float) -> float:
        if not 0.0 <= v <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"Score must be between 0.0 and 1.0, got {v}")
        return v


# ── §4 Top-level report ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────


class CulpritReport(BaseModel):
    """
    Final output of a Culprit debug run (§4, §12).

    adjudications collects every Adjudication produced across all attempts.
    adjudicator_available is False when watsonx.ai was unreachable (§12).
    """

    status: ReportStatus
    bug: Bug
    root_cause: Optional[RootCause] = None  # None if the run aborted before tracing
    fix: Optional[Fix] = None
    regression_test: Optional[RegressionTest] = None
    attempts: list[Attempt]
    elapsed_seconds: float
    bobcoins_used: float
    adjudications: list[Adjudication]
    adjudicator_available: bool

+"""
+Culprit domain exceptions.
+
+Each exception corresponds to an explicit edge case in §7.
+Catching code must not swallow these silently — they propagate to the
+orchestrator which maps them to a CulpritReport status.
+"""
+
+
+class CulpritError(Exception):
+    """Base class for all Culprit domain errors."""
+
+
+class SubagentError(CulpritError):
+    """Bob returned malformed JSON after the allowed retry (E2)."""
+
+
+class BudgetExhausted(CulpritError):
+    """Bobcoin budget MAX_BOBCOIN_PER_RUN exceeded (E4)."""
+
+
+class AuthError(CulpritError):
+    """Auth token acquisition or refresh failed (E7)."""
+
+
+class UnreachableError(CulpritError):
+    """Target URL timed out or DNS-resolved to nothing (E8)."""
+
+
+class BugNotObservable(CulpritError):
+    """URL returned 200; the bug could not be reproduced (E9)."""
+
+
+class MissingCodebaseError(CulpritError):
+    """Bug spans a codebase not provided to the run (E10)."""
+
+
+class ConfigurationError(CulpritError):
+    """Required configuration (env var, CLI flag combination) is missing or invalid."""
+
+
+class WatsonxError(CulpritError):
+    """watsonx.ai call failed (timeout, auth, malformed output); caller fails open (§12)."""
+

+class BobShellError(CulpritError):
